mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the same month of FEDFUNDS spike, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightening reduces growth expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat during the two-month UNRATE expansion, with p-value > 0.05 in a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (household spending index) above its 12-month moving average predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals stronger consumer demand.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05) during the HOUST expansion episode.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% over two months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing output implies contractionary expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the INDPRO decline, with p-value > 0.05 in a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 shows a positive 5-day forward return as dual inflation and policy tightening are mispriced.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS up >0.25% and CPIAUCSL up >0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative or zero, with p-value > 0.05 in a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 130,000 in a month coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market weakness dampens investor optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or flat during the employment contraction, with p-value > 0.05 over the past 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows at an annualized rate above 3% for three consecutive quarters, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as strong aggregate demand supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 3% for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the high-GDP-growth period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of 5% or more indicates weak consumer spending, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return in a deflationary regime.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by ≥5% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the RSAFS decline, with p-value > 0.05 in a 2-year horizon.
